name: Sangen-Jaya
tagline: Shibuya in 7 minutes and Shinjuku in 17 minutes. Served by 2 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥90,000 to ¥100,000.
summary: The station is in Setagaya City, served by Tokyu Den-en-toshi Line and Tokyu Setagaya Line. Journey times to the main business districts are 31 minutes to Otemachi, 17 minutes to Shinjuku, 7 minutes to Shibuya and 33 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥90,000 to ¥100,000. The station stands 32.2 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 8.3 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 32.2 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 25 m to 33.3 m, a difference of 8.3 m. These figures were read from the elevation API of the Geospatial Information Authority of Japan at nine points: the station itself and eight compass directions 400 m out.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 5 fall inside the area, and the deepest projection among them is 0.5 to 3 m. The projected depth differs block by block within the same station area, so check the ward hazard map for the specific address. Inland flooding from overwhelmed drains has no nationwide map; each ward publishes its own, and that is worth reading as well.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 20 clinics and 22 pharmacies. Facilities recorded as hospitals lie at 青葉会青葉病院, about 117 m away and 歯科, about 151 m away. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 2 lines serve the station: Tokyu Den-en-toshi Line and Tokyu Setagaya Line. Both lines are run by Tokyu, so a fault affecting that company can stop them together. Scored out of 100 from the number of lines and the spread of operators, transfer convenience here comes to 52.

rentRange.note: One room ¥90,000 to ¥100,000, 1K ¥100,000 to ¥110,000, 1LDK ¥190,000 to ¥200,000 and 2LDK ¥260,000 to ¥270,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥90,000 to ¥100,000. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.
